2. In brief, the facts of the case are that on 10.04.2023, petitioner was going to Outram Lane Mukherjee Nagar for work on his motorcycle bearing No. DL8SDA 2333 and at about 9.30 a.m. when he reached near T-Point, New Life Hospital,
suddenly a TSR bearing number DLIRU1455 driven by its driver in rash and negligent manner came from front side and hit his motorcycle with great force, due to which he fell down on road and sustained injuries on his left leg.

He was taken to New Life Hospital, where after first aid he was referred to Trauma Centre, Civil Lines,
Delhi for further treatment.

3. A criminal case FIR No. 0449/2023 under Section 279/338 IPC was registered in PS Mukherjee Nagar and charge sheet under Section 173 Cr.PC under the above FIR was filed against Ram Nandan Mistri (respondent no.1 / driver of the vehicle in question) for causing the accident.
4. Respondents no. 1 and 2 have not filed any reply / written statement despite giving sufficient opportunities.

Accordingly, their right to file reply / written statement was struck off vide order dated 15.05.2024.
5.

In its reply / written statement, the respondent no. 3 / Ins. Co. denied its liability on the ground that vehicle in question was not involved in the alleged accident as Amit vs Ram Nandan Mistri on 6 November, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/4189254/
3
there is delay in lodging the FIR which creates suspicion as to the veracity of the alleged accident.
However, it is not disputed that the vehicle in question was duly insured with it as on the date of accident.

After completion of the pleadings, following issues were framed vide order dated 15.05.2024: -
1.

Whether injured/petitioner Amit suffered grievous injuries in a vehicular accident occurred on 10.04.2023 at 09:30 AM at BB Marg, T Point, New Life Hospital,
Outram Lane, Delhi, within the jurisdiction of PS Mukherjee Nagar, Delhi, due to rash and negligent driving of vehicle i.e. TSR bearing registration No. DLIRU1455 by respondent no. 1 (Ram Nandan Mistri)?

OPP. 
2. Whether the petitioner/injured is entitled to compensation if so, what amount and from whom of respondents?

OPP. 
3. Relief.
7.

Respondent no. 3 did not lead any evidence and request made for closing RE.
Neither respondent no. 1 nor respondent no. 2 have filed any evidence by way of affidavit nor they have examined any other witness.

Accordingly, RE on behalf of all the respondents was closed vide order dated 24.09.2025.
8.
I have heard ld. counsels appearing on behalf of petitioner and respondent no. 3 and gone through the record carefully.
None has appeared on behalf of respondents no.1 and 2 for advancing final argument either in person or through video conferencing nor any written submission filed on their behalf.
Accordingly, material available on record, on their behalf, would be considered as their submissions.
9. My issue-wise findings are as under:-

ISSUE No.1 Whether injured/petitioner Amit suffered grievous injuries in a vehicular accident occurred on 10.04.2023 at 09:30 AM at BB Marg, T Point, New Life Hospital, MACT no. 466/23 Amit Vs. Ram Nandan Mistri & Ors.

The onus to prove this issue was upon the petitioner and to prove that he suffered injuries due to rash and negligent driving on the part of respondent no. 1, petitioner examined himself as PW1 and tendered his evidence by way of affidavit Ex. PW1/A.
Petitioner

/ PW1 deposed that on 10.04.2024 at about 9:30 a.m. he was going to Outram Lane Mukherjee Nagar for work on motorcycle bearing No. DL8SDA 2333 and when he reached near T Point, New Life Hospital, then all of a sudden, from the front side, a TSR bearing number DLIRU1455 driven by its driver in rash and negligent manner hit him with great force, due to which he fell on road and received crush injuries on his left leg.
He further deposed that driver of offending vehicle took him to New Life Hospital, where he was administered with first aid, and then referred to Trauma Centre, Civil Lines Delhi and treated upon.

PW1 further deposed that the accident occurred due to sole negligence driving of the driver of the offending vehicle and driver of the vehicle in question assured him that he will bear all expenses of treatment but he failed to do so.

Though, PW1 has been cross examined by the respondent no. 3 / Ins. Co. but nothing material has come on record to disbelieve the testimony of PW1, with regard to rash and negligent driving by respondent no. 1, as petitioner being injured is natural eye-witness of accident and petitioner/PW1 has not at all been cross examined by the respondents no. 1 and 2.

Further, respondent no. 1 being driver of offending vehicle was himself material witness to throw light by testifying as to how and under what circumstances and manner, the accident has taken place but he opted not to enter into the witness box and did not lead any evidence and there is nothing on record to show that the petitioner had any enmity with the driver of the offending vehicle so as to falsely implicate him in MACT no.
466/23

SUNIL Page 6 KUMAR 2025.11.06 14:22:22 +0530 this case, meaning thereby that respondents no. 1 and 2 have nothing to say about the rash and negligence on the part of respondent no. 1 and the manner in which the accident had occurred.
Further, the DAR collectively Ex. PW1/4 shows that respondent no.1 was charge sheeted by the police for offences punishable under Section 279/338 IPC.
Apart from deposition of PW1, the fact that petitioner suffered injuries in the accident is also supported by his MLC filed along with the DAR.
Respondent no. 1 has not placed on record any document to disprove the factum of rash and negligent driving by him.
Further, there is nothing on record which shows that respondent no. 1 has ever approached to any higher authority against his false implication in the present case.

Relying upon the judgment of Mahila Dhanvanti and Ors Vs. Phulwant Mahendra Singh, Miscellaneous Appeal no.239/1992 decided by Hon'ble Madhya Pradesh High Court on 29.07.1993 in which it is held as under: -

entities.text: Mahila Dhanvanti and Ors Vs. Phulwant Mahendra Singh, Miscellaneous Appeal no.239/1992
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: "The plaintiff can prove the accident but cannot prove how it happened to establish negligence.
This hardship is to be avoided by applying the principle of res ipsa loquitur.

The general purport of the words res ipsa loquitur is that the accident speaks for itself or tells its own story".
Amit vs Ram Nandan Mistri on 6 November, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/4189254/
5
Thus, Claims Tribunal while dealing with the law of torts in motor accident cases applies the principle of "res ipsa loquitur".

Considering all this, it stands proved that petitioner suffered grievous injuries in a vehicular accident occurred on 0.04.2023 at 09:30 AM at BB Marg, T Point, New Life Hospital, Outram Lane, Delhi, due to rash and negligent driving of vehicle i.e. TSR bearing registration No. DLIRU1455 by respondent no. 1.
Issue no. 1 is accordingly decided in favour of petitioner and against the respondent.

10.
As far as right to claim compensation is concerned, being injured, petitioner is well within his rights to claim compensation from the respondents.
Accordingly, the question of right of the petitioner for claiming of compensation is decided in favour of the petitioner.

Now, coming to the issue with respect to the quantum of compensation is to be adjudicated and below are the finding: -
11. Section 168 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988, mandate the Tribunal to hold an inquiry into claims under section 166 and to determine the amount of compensation which appears to be just and reasonable.

The Hon'ble Supreme Court in "Sarla Verma v. Delhi Transport Corporation" (2009),
held as under:
"Just compensation" is adequate compensation which is fair and equitable, on the facts and circumstances of the case, to make good the loss suffered as a result of the wrong, as far as money can do so, by applying the well settled principles relating to award of compensation.

Except deposition of petitioner, there is no evidence to verify that any amount has been spent on special diet and conveyance etc.

However, keeping in view the nature of injuries sustained by the petitioner, the period of his hospitalization as well as the surgeries and procedures undergone by him and the record of his follow up treatment, this tribunal is of the opinion that the petitioner must have incurred expenses on special diet required for his speedy recovery and conveyance.
Accordingly, Rs.15,000/- each towards special diet and conveyance are awarded to the petitioner.

13. It is a matter of record that during the pendency of the case, the petitioner was referred to Aruna Asaf Ali Govt. Hospital, 5 Rajpur Road, Delhi for assessment of permanent disability and a certificate received on record, as per which petitioner has suffered 5% permanent disability in relation to his left lower limb i.e. amputation of 4 th & 5th toe of left foot.
Since the permanent disability of petitioner has been assessed by the government hospital / disability board, this Tribunal has no reason to disbelieve the disability certificate received on record.
14. Though, it is claimed that petitioner was earning Rs. 30,000/- per month but except deposition of petitioner, there is nothing on record to prove his such income on record.
Further, petitioner in his cross examination admitted that he is illiterate and has no document to show his employment and earning.

During the arguments, Ld. Counsel for petitioner submitted that since the petitioner has suffered permanent disability, loss to future income may be calculated as per Minimum Wages Act, prevalent at the time of accident.

Considering the facts and circumstances of the case and the fact that petitioner MACT no. 466/23 Amit Vs. Ram Nandan Mistri & Ors.

18.
Admittedly, the vehicle was insured.

However, respondent no. 3 / Ins. Co. has taken certain technical pleas including that there is delay in filing the FIR but no witness has been examined nor any document has been placed on record to support the contention that vehicle in question was not involved in the accident.
Admittedly respondent no. 3 / Ins. Co. has no statutory defence.
Even otherwise, it is well settled law that delay in lodging FIR can not be a ground to throw away the case of claimant in MACT no. 466/23 Amit Vs. Ram Nandan Mistri & Ors.

OPP. 
2. Whether the petitioner/injured is entitled to compensation if so, what amount and from whom of respondents?
Now, coming to the issue with respect to the quantum of compensation is to be adjudicated and below are the finding: -
11. Section 168 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988, mandate the Tribunal to hold an inquiry into claims under section 166 and to determine the amount of compensation which appears to be just and reasonable.
opennyai_summary.facts:
Further, respondent no. 1 being driver of offending vehicle was himself material witness to throw light by testifying as to how and under what circumstances and manner, the accident has taken place but he opted not to enter into the witness box and did not lead any evidence and there is nothing on record to show that the petitioner had any enmity with the driver of the offending vehicle so as to falsely implicate him in MACT no.
466/23
As far as right to claim compensation is concerned, being injured, petitioner is well within his rights to claim compensation from the respondents.
opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
Respondent no. 1 has not placed on record any document to disprove the factum of rash and negligent driving by him.
Further, there is nothing on record which shows that respondent no. 1 has ever approached to any higher authority against his false implication in the present case.
As far as loss of income during the treatment is concerned, as stated above petitioner has suffered 5% permanent disability and considering the same, it is presumed that petitioner would have not been able to continue his work for about 3 months.
16. As far as loss of income on account of loss of future earning due to disability is concerned, There is no dispute with regard to the disability suffered by the petitioner and no rebuttal evidence has brought on record with regard to the disability and hence considering the 5% permanent disability,
that two amputation of toe, no doubt, this kind of disability would hamper his day to day activity and work for gain.
Accordingly, the functional disability is taken as 2.5% qua whole body for calculating the loss of earning capacity.
Accordingly, this amount of Rs.1,23,050.76p, is allowed to petitioner, as loss of future earnings, due to permanent disability.
No tax is deducted since the said income of petitioner is not taxable.
Admittedly, the vehicle was insured.
Admittedly respondent no. 3 / Ins. Co. has no statutory defence.
Even otherwise, it is well settled law that delay in lodging FIR can not be a ground to throw away the case of claimant in MACT no. 466/23 Amit Vs. Ram Nandan Mistri & Ors.
8 conditions prevailing in our society where one can not expect common man to rush to police station for registration of FIR immediately after the accident.
Further, no material has come on record which shows that there is any breach of terms and conditions of insurance policy of offending vehicle.
The allegations levelled in the written statement howsoever strong that may be, cannot take place of proof particularly when insurance company despite having raised the issue has not led any evidence on such aspect.
Hence,
merely taking the plea, insurnce company cannot escape from its liabilities.
In view of the above and since the respondent no.3 / Ins. Co. has failed to establish any statutory defence, it is liable to indemnify the owner / insured and to pay compensation to the petitioner.
opennyai_summary.arguments: During the arguments, Ld. Counsel for petitioner submitted that since the petitioner has suffered permanent disability, loss to future income may be calculated as per Minimum Wages Act, prevalent at the time of accident.

Issue no. 2 is accordingly decided in favour of petitioner and against the respondent no.3 / Ins. Co.
holding that petitioner is entitled to get compensation from respondent no.3 / Ins. Co.
